claims.text: The initial material is a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
Conventional processing of the W–Cu composite produces significant phase separation and interfacial void formation.
Rapid SPS with a tailored heating-cooling profile will minimize diffusion time during sintering.
High heat flux and irradiation exposure are relevant service conditions for joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components.
Suppressing W–Cu interfacial diffusion will reduce phase separation.
Suppressing W–Cu interfacial diffusion will decrease interfacial void formation.
Rapid SPS reduces the time available for thermal diffusion at the W–Cu interface.
Reduced interfacial diffusion limits liquid-phase formation that would otherwise cause phase separation and void nucleation.
Reduced phase separation and void formation maintain continuous thermal pathways between W and Cu.
Maintaining continuous thermal pathways enhances the composite's thermal conductivity.
The SPS-treated W–Cu composite will have a more homogeneous microstructure and fewer interfacial voids than the conventionally sintered control.
The SPS-treated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the conventionally sintered composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The SPS-treated composite will resist irradiation-induced degradation better than the conventionally sintered composite.
Slower conventional heating and cooling cause significant interfacial diffusion, phase separation, and void formation that correlate with lower thermal conductivity.
Subsequent high-temperature exposure may alter or destabilize the sintered microstructure.
SPS processing parameters must be tightly controlled for the proposed effect to occur.
Scaling and sensitivity to processing parameters may introduce variability.
SEM/EDS can be used to assess phase homogeneity and interfacial microstructure in the proposed comparison.
Failure to obtain both reduced void or segregation defects and higher thermal conductivity relative to the conventional control would falsify the hypothesis.
